patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Nextiva and Talkdesk share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Nextiva only if your buying job matches “SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/mo” rather than Talkdesk's shape. Choose Talkdesk only if your buying job matches “Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital Essentials from $85/user/mo; Voice $105; Elite $165” rather than Nextiva's shape. Workflow advantage: Nextiva leans business-phone, team-communication; Talkdesk leans sales-calling. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Nextiva and Talkdesk share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Nextiva is SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/month annual, with messaging apps including WhatsApp; Talkdesk is Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital Essentials from $85/user/mo; Voice $105; Elite $165; Industry Clouds from $225..
- Company-size focus: Nextiva (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Talkdesk (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Nextiva-leaning business-phone, team-communication vs Talkdesk-leaning sales-calling.
- Researched limits: Nextiva — Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included; Talkdesk — Digital and Voice Essentials are channel-siloed — true omnichannel starts at Elite ($165).

Limitations — Nextiva: Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included; Analytics and AI assistance require Scale / higher plans or XBert add-on from $99/mo; Talkdesk: Digital and Voice Essentials are channel-siloed — true omnichannel starts at Elite ($165); CXA AI (Copilot/Autopilot/Navigator) is typically add-on priced on top of CX Cloud seats.

Poor-fit cases: Nextiva is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included · Talkdesk is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Digital and Voice Essentials are channel-siloed — true omnichannel starts at Elite ($165) · Avoid Nextiva if you actually need Talkdesk's motion (Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital Essentials from $85/user/mo; Voice $105; )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
